rule: order = the order of the code slides of the deck; the page tab lists the examples by name in this order; each runs as setup + listing, with the library defined in the page

setup.code:
# setup: the chapter library of the page (L = the chapter 9 library, with the recorded runs of Bitcoin Core 31.1 and the census of two blocks, R, R2 and C); the page boots these names
import sen0401_ch09_lib_v1_0_1 as L
R, R2, C = L.run(), L.run2(), L.census()
B = C['blocks']

examples.name: A fee is a difference, not a field
examples.code:
# An independent parser reads the raw bytes of one transaction.
a = R['fee_arith']
t = L.parse_tx(a['tx']['hex'])
# It finds inputs, outputs and a lock time, but no fee field.
has_fee = 'fee' in t
n_in, n_out = len(t['vin']), len(t['vout'])
# The fee is what is left: inputs minus outputs.
outs = sum(o['value'] for o in t['vout'])
ins = round(a['inputs_btc'] * 1e8)
fee = ins - outs
print(has_fee, fee)

examples.name: A forgotten change output pays the miner
examples.code:
# A payment spends 20 coins, sends 1 and forgets its change.
a = R['fee_arith']
why = a['testmempoolaccept']['reject-reason']
# The node's error text names the safety limit maxfeerate.
err = a['sendrawtransaction_default']['error']
guard = 'maxfeerate' in err
# Mined with the limit lifted, the miner gets subsidy plus fee.
bs = a['blockstats']
pay = bs['subsidy'] + bs['totalfee']
paid = a['coinbase_out_sat'] == pay
print(why, guard, paid)

examples.name: A signed payment cannot be edited
examples.code:
# One payment as signed, and a copy with its output cut.
w = R2['tamper']
o, t = w['original'], w['tampered']
# The node rejects the copy: the signature covers the amounts.
ok = [o['allowed'], t['allowed']]
why = t['reject-reason'].split(' (')[0]
# The cut is the extra fee; only the spender could add it.
d = w['output0_original_sat']
cut = d - w['output0_tampered_sat']
print(ok, cut)

examples.name: Size, weight and virtual size
examples.code:
# One payment of the test node, parsed from its hex text.
x = R['rbf']['t1']
t = L.parse_tx(x['hex'])
# Witness bytes count a quarter, so weight is not size.
sizes = [t['base_size'], t['size']]
wv = [t['weight'], t['vsize']]
# Virtual size is weight over four, rounded up.
ratio = round(x['vsize'] / x['weight'], 4)
print(sizes + wv)

examples.name: A fee rate and its units
examples.code:
# The rate is the fee divided by the virtual size.
x = R['rbf']['t1']
rate = x['fee_sat'] / x['vsize']
# Coins per thousand bytes convert to satoshis per byte.
a = float(L.btc_kvb_to_sat_vb('0.00006570'))
b = float(L.btc_kvb_to_sat_vb('0.00001225'))
# Two spellings of one rate give one fee: mind the units.
p = R['units']['fee_rate_sat_vb_10']['ok']['fee']
q = R['units']['feeRate_btc_kvb_0.0001']['ok']['fee']
same = p == q
print(rate, a, b, same)

examples.name: Space in a block is limited
examples.code:
# The limit is a consensus constant in the saved source.
src = 'core_src_consensus_consensus.h'
limit = int(L.const(src, 'MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT'))
# Block 840,000 weighs almost exactly as much as the limit.
w = B['840000']['weight']
share = round(100 * w / limit, 2)
print(w, limit, share)

examples.name: The minimum relay fee
examples.code:
# Three payments of 141 bytes, paying 8, 14 and 15 satoshis.
m = list(R['minrelay'].values())[:3]
fees = [v['fee_sat'] for v in m]
# Only the last is taken; the node's floor is 0.1 per byte.
taken = [v['result']['ok'][0]['allowed'] for v in m]
floor = R2['mempool_min']['minrelaytxfee'] * 1e8 / 1000
# 141 bytes at that floor cost 14.1, so 15 is the least.
need = int(141 * floor) + 1
print(fees, taken, need)

examples.name: Dust and the wallet's own floor
examples.code:
# The wallet refuses 0.5 and 0.1 satoshis per byte, takes 1.
w = R2['wallet_min']
ks = ['fee_rate_0.5', 'fee_rate_0.1', 'fee_rate_1']
wal = ['ok' in w[k] for k in ks]
# Dust costs more to spend than it holds: (size + 67) x 3.
sz = {'P2WPKH': 31, 'P2TR': 43, 'P2A': 13}
dust = {k: (n + 67) * 3 for k, n in sz.items()}
print(dust)

examples.name: An estimate needs history
examples.code:
# A node with no blocks answers an estimate with an error.
f = R['estimate_fresh']['ok']['errors'][0]
# After 120 rounds of test traffic it has history to use.
n = R['estimate']['rounds']
E = R['estimate']['results']
# Estimates for targets of 2, 6 and 25 blocks, in sat per byte.
keys = ['2_default', '6_default', '25_default']
rates = [round(E[k]['ok']['feerate'] * 1e5, 3) for k in keys]
print(rates)

examples.name: How far the estimator can see
examples.code:
# A target of 144 blocks is answered with the 60 it can see.
E = R['estimate']['results']
seen = E['144_default']['ok']['blocks']
# The default mode gives the economical answer at every target.
ts = (2, 6, 25, 144)
eco = [E[f'{t}_economical'] for t in ts]
dft = [E[f'{t}_default'] for t in ts]
same = eco == dft
# The cautious conservative mode differs at 144 blocks.
cons = E['144_default'] == E['144_conservative']
print(seen, same, cons)

examples.name: Two blocks, two fee markets
examples.code:
# The census holds the 599 best-paying payments of two blocks.
a = L.census_stats(840000)
b = L.census_stats(971489)
# The median fee rate fell from over a thousand to three.
n = a['n']
med = [a['median_rate'], b['median_rate']]
print(med)

examples.name: The opt-in replacement signal
examples.code:
# A low enough input sequence number signals replaceability.
sig = L.rbf_signal
flags = [sig([0xfffffffd]), sig([0xfffffffe])]
mixed = sig([0xffffffff, 0xfffffffd])
# Most payments of the halving block signal; fewer later.
a = L.census_stats(840000)
b = L.census_stats(971489)
share = [a['signal_rbf'], b['signal_rbf']]
print(flags, mixed, share)

examples.name: A replacement must pay enough
examples.code:
# A payment of 564 satoshis meets four conflicting copies.
X = R['rbf']
ks = ['lower_fee', 'equal_fee']
ks += ['short_by_one', 'exactly_enough']
# Each copy has its own fee; the node accepts or refuses.
fees = [X[k]['fee_sat'] for k in ks]
taken = ['ok' in X[k]['result'] for k in ks]
# Rule: old fee plus new size at the incremental rate.
need = L.min_replacement_fee(564, 141)
print(fees, taken)

examples.name: Full replacement is the default
examples.code:
# The first payment has a final sequence: it never signalled.
x = R['rbf']
seq = x['t1']['sequence']
# Yet a conflicting payment replaced it: full replacement is on.
full = x['fullrbf_flag']
swapped = 'ok' in x['t2']['result']
# The switch to turn that off was removed in 29.0.
o = R2['removed_option']
m = o['message']
gone = (o['exit_code'], 'mempoolfullrbf=0' in m)
print(full, seq, swapped, gone)

examples.name: Paying the payee twice
examples.code:
# Three versions of one payment, each replacing the last.
h = R2['hazard']
i = h['inputs']
# Versions 0 and 1 conflict, 1 and 2 conflict, 0 and 2 do not.
c01 = L.conflict(i['v0'], i['v1'])
c12 = L.conflict(i['v1'], i['v2'])
c02 = L.conflict(i['v0'], i['v2'])
# So 0 and 2 can both be mined: the payee is paid twice.
asked = h['payee_asked_sat']
got = h['payee_received_sat']
print(asked, got, [c01, c12, c02])

examples.name: A child lifts its parent
examples.code:
# A parent pays 141 satoshis, its child 14,100; 141 bytes each.
w = R['ancestor_mining']['cpfp_wins']
E = w['mempoolentries']
fee = w['fees_sat']
# Alone, the parent pays 1 per byte and the child 100.
alone = [fee[k] / E[k]['vsize'] for k in ('P', 'C')]
# The miner prices the pair as one package.
c = E['P']
fee_c = c['fees']['chunk'] * 1e8
pair = round(fee_c / (c['chunkweight'] / 4), 2)
print(alone, pair)

examples.name: A weak child does not help
examples.code:
# The child pays only 5 satoshis per byte; A waits too.
w = R['ancestor_mining']['cpfp_loses']
E, fee = w['mempoolentries'], w['fees_sat']
# Together parent and child pay about 3 per byte, below A.
c = E['P']
tot = fee['P'] + fee['C']
pair = round(tot / (c['chunkweight'] / 4), 2)
# Miners took A and left the pair out of the block.
first = [w[k]['txid'] in w['block_txids'] for k in ('A', 'P')]
print(pair, first)

examples.name: Package relay
examples.code:
# A parent pays 8 satoshis; alone it misses the floor of 15.
p = R['package']
solo = p['v2_parent_alone']['ok'][0]['reject-details']
# Its child, sent first, fails: the parent is unknown.
alone = L.reason(p['child_alone'])
# As a package the pair is judged together and accepted.
msg = p['submitpackage_v2']['ok']['package_msg']
print(msg)

examples.name: Cluster limits
examples.code:
# The mempool groups connected payments into clusters with limits.
c = R['cluster']
mi = c['mempoolinfo']
lim = (mi['limitclustercount'], mi['limitclustersize'])
# A chain of 65: 64 accepted, the next one refused.
ch = c['chain']
tried = (ch['attempted'], ch['accepted'])
why = L.reason(ch['first_refusal'])
# The old 25-ancestor limit is gone: a chain of 26 passes.
ok26 = ch['accepted_26th']
print(lim, tried, why, ok26)

examples.name: Mempool size and expiry
examples.code:
# The defaults are constants in the saved Bitcoin Core source.
o = 'core_src_kernel_mempool_options.h'
size = int(L.const(o, 'DEFAULT_MAX_MEMPOOL_SIZE_MB'))
# A waiting payment is dropped after 336 hours, which is 14 days.
hours = int(L.const(o, 'DEFAULT_MEMPOOL_EXPIRY_HOURS'))
days = hours // 24
print(size, hours, days)

examples.name: A big child pins its parent
examples.code:
# A parent paying 705 satoshis gets a child of 90,012 bytes or 885.
P = R['pinning']
v2, v3 = P['v2'], P['v3']
# To replace the parent, pay for the whole pinned family.
cost2 = v2['replacement_enough']['fee_sat']
cost3 = v3['replacement_enough']['fee_sat']
# A capped version 3 child cuts the price about 88-fold.
ratio = round(cost2 / cost3)
print(cost2, cost3, ratio)

examples.name: TRUC limits on a family
examples.code:
# A version 3 child may be 1,000 bytes at most; 1,350 fails.
t = R['truc']
why = L.reason
bad = 'TRUC-violation' in why(t['big_child']['result'])
# A small child of 141 bytes is accepted without trouble.
ok = 'ok' in t['child1']['result']
# A second child replaces the first only at a higher rate.
r1 = why(t['sibling_same_rate']['result'])
r2 = t['sibling_higher_rate']['result']
ev = ['sibling eviction' in r1, 'ok' in r2]
print(bad, ok, ev)

examples.name: Pay to anchor
examples.code:
# A version 3 parent pays no fee and has one anchor output.
p = R['package']
par = L.parse_tx(p['truc_parent']['hex'])
o = par['vout'][0]
anchor = (o['spk'], o['value'], par['version'])
# Alone it is refused; with its child it is accepted.
alone = L.reason(p['parent_alone'])
msg = p['submitpackage_truc']['ok']['package_msg']
# The child spends the anchor with an empty witness.
kid = L.parse_tx(p['anchor_child']['hex'])
empty = [v['witness'] for v in kid['vin']].count([])
print(anchor)

examples.name: The carve-out limit
examples.code:
# The extra descendant size is a constant in the Core source.
p = 'core_src_policy_policy.h'
lim = int(L.const(p, 'EXTRA_DESCENDANT_TX_SIZE_LIMIT'))
# The book states another number; the saved text confirms it.
bk = 'book_ch09_fees.adoc'
said = 'additional transaction up to 1,000 vbytes'
book = L.has(bk, said)
# Release 31.0 removed the rule with the cluster mempool.
n = 'core_relnotes_31.0.html'
gone = L.has(n, 'removed from the mempool logic')
print(lim, book, gone)

examples.name: Fees against the subsidy
examples.code:
# Two blocks of the census: halving block 840,000 and 971,489.
a, b = B['840000']['extras'], B['971489']['extras']
fees, reward = a['totalFees'], a['reward']
# In the halving block the subsidy was only the remainder.
subsidy = reward - fees
# Fees were nearly all of one reward, a sliver of the other.
ratio = [z['totalFees'] / z['reward'] for z in (a, b)]
share = [round(100 * r, 2) for r in ratio]
print(share)

examples.name: Odds of winning a sniping race
examples.code:
# The chance to win a re-mining race is (x/(1-x)) squared.
xs = [0.1, 0.3, 0.45, 0.5]
odds = [L.snipe_probability(x) for x in xs]
# At 45 percent two in three; at half the rate, certain.
pct = [round(100 * p, 2) for p in odds]
print(pct)

examples.name: Wallets lock to the chain tip
examples.code:
# Sixty test payments: how far below the tip is each lock time?
s = R['sniping']['samples']
gap = sorted(z['tip'] - z['locktime'] for z in s)
# Most sit at the tip; a few are set back by some blocks.
at_tip = gap.count(0)
back = [g for g in gap if g]
# A payment is not final in the block of its lock time.
late = L.is_final(100001, 100001, [0xfffffffd])
print(at_tip, back, late)
